predecessors.name: Tibet
predecessors.text: Tsang and Ü, the Tsangpa realm with Shigatse: 'The Tsangpa stronghold, Shigatse, was captured after a long and bloody siege in March 1642'

successors.name: Tibet
successors.text: Lhasa and Central Tibet, left to the Tibetan government (Ganden Phodrang) when the Khoshut khan died in December 1717; the Dzungars held it under occupation from 1717 to 1720

successors.name: Qing dynasty
successors.text: Amdo, made the province of Qinghai in 1724

ledger.x: 1637: Güshi Khan defeats Choghtu near Qinghai Lake and holds the Kokonor country.
1641: the king of Beri is crushed.
1642: the Tsangpa realm passes to Güshi.
13 April 1642: the 5th Dalai Lama proclaims Güshi khan of Tibet and the Khoshut Khanate is established.
December 1717: Lhazang Khan dies at the Potala.
December 1717: Khoshut rule in Central Tibet ends.

December 1717: Kham leaves the Khoshuts with the khanate of Tibet. fx-48 (3 Nov 2026): the dissolve used to release Kham with everything else in December 1717; with the dissolve moved to 1724 for Qinghai this loss keeps that behaviour.
1724: the rebellion is over and Qinghai is a province.

1724: the Khoshuts of Qinghai end when the Qing make Amdo the province of Qinghai ('The Qing made the region of Amdo into the province of Qinghai in 1724'). fx-48 (3 Nov 2026): this was dated December 1717 and took Ü-Tsang, Kham and Qinghai together ('the collapse of the Khoshut Khanate', Dzungar conquest of Tibet…

wars.name: Güshi Khan's invasion of Qinghai
wars.outcome: Khoshut victory in 1637 over Choghtu Khong Tayiji, whom the Khoshut page has led a 30,000 strong army and the Güshi page calls a Khalkha leader.

wars.name: Güshi Khan's conquest of Kham and Tsang
wars.outcome: The king of Beri was crushed in 1640-41, Kham subdued by 1641 and Shigatse taken in March 1642; the Dalai Lama proclaimed Güshi khan of Tibet on 13 April 1642.

wars.name: Khoshut expedition to Bhutan
wars.outcome: 'Güshi Khan and the regent sent several hundred Mongol and Tibetan troops into Bhutan in 1644'; no result or land is named.

wars.name: Dzungar conquest of Tibet
wars.outcome: Dzungar victory: Tseren Dhondup took Lhasa on 30 November 1717 and Lhazang Khan died in December; the Khoshut Khanate collapsed.

certainty.note: The Khoshut lands are a mountain and plateau realm whose frontiers no page opened describes; Qinghai, Kham and Tibet are named regions, not lines.
Only the 1723 rising and the 1724 province are dated; the Kokonor Khoshut line in 1718-1722 is a bridge between the fall of Lhasa and the Qing province.
